clue.text: The wrong plot?

parts.note: read as a burial plot dug in the wrong place, it becomes a serious mistake: plot as a patch of graveyard

explanation.definitionFit: A serious mistake is a blunder of real consequence, and the clue jokes that a burial plot is the 'grave' half of it.

clue.text: Soil is reduced to powder

explanation.definitionFit: Earth underfoot is the land's surface, and coffee beans milled fine have been crushed, the past participle of grind.

clue.text: Record-books?

parts.note: not ledgers of results but bound collections, of vinyl records or of photos and stamps

explanation.definitionFit: LP collections and photo scrapbooks are both books that keep records, in the two senses of record.

clue.text: Senior politician seen — am startled by changed appearance

indicators.note: letters whose appearance has been changed are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is startled by how much a person they have just seen has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by changed appearance' tells you to rearrange SEEN AM STARTLED; 'seen' looks like part of the definition but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran respected statesman, often retired, is a figure of experience in public life.

clue.text: The kind of glances you might expect from a gunman?

definitions.text: The kind of glances you might expect from a gunman?

parts.words: The kind of glances you might expect from a gunman?
parts.note: glances here are not looks but bullets glancing off surfaces and bouncing away

explanation.definitionFit: Bullets that rebound off a wall or rock are said to glance off, a gunfire bounce.

clue.text: Proprietor is new or changed

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed into another order

explanation.surface: A proprietor has been replaced, or is new.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a proprietor is the person who possesses a business or property.

clue.text: Of the ear — or if pressure is applied, of the eye

indicators.note: the clue says adding the letter for pressure gives the eye word, so the answer is that word with it taken away

parts.note: optic is the adjective meaning of the eye
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: An anatomy note about an ear word turning into an eye word when squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue states it backwards: the answer plus P gives OPTIC, so remove the P from OPTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical adjective for the auditory organ, as in otic drops, comes from Greek ous, ear.

clue.text: In turkey, I keep to the shade — as told — yet flag

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so a word sounding like the shade is wanted

parts.note: a shade is a colour, which sounds the same as the American spelling

explanation.surface: A traveller in Turkey keeps out of the sun yet is drooping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turkey' looks like the bird but is the country; the answer takes the American spelling, sounding just like the British one.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national banner of three bands is the classic three-coloured standard.

clue.text: Joins swindler at exhibition centre on back street

parts.note: a con is a con man, a swindler
the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre near Birmingham

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for street is turned round

explanation.surface: A trickster meets up with people at a show venue in a side street.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEC is Britain's National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham; 'back' reverses ST to TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to couple two things is to link them up.

clue.text: Leave sailor, as ray Charles demanded

parts.note: to hit the road is to set off or depart
jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A request that a seaman go away, echoing a famous song.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray Charles had a 1961 hit telling a man to leave: the song title is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer's best-known order to a departing lover was the refrain of his chart hit.

clue.text: Alternatively, the couch could be circular

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a couch is a bed

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the sofa might be round instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: round, shaped like a sphere or disc.

clue.text: State one's requirement

explanation.definitionFit: A state of health or repair, and a stipulation someone insists on before agreeing.

clue.text: Almost without feeling, Eric is painting by numbers

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: numb means without feeling

explanation.surface: Eric, nearly unfeeling, does a paint-by-numbers picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts NUMB to NUM; ERIC is given as is.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressed in digits or figures, as opposed to words.

clue.text: Price for a short holiday in vermin-infested accommodation

indicators.note: the price is around the break, as the payment for it wraps it

parts.note: a rate is a price charged
HOL is the British short form of holiday

explanation.surface: A cheap break turns out to be in a dingy, rodent-ridden place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' places HOL, British slang shortening of holiday, inside RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A squalid dwelling compared to the burrow of a rodent: a dump.

clue.text: Extended time in jail before journalist is free

parts.note: a stretch is slang for a prison sentence
ED, short for editor, is a journalist
out means free, released

explanation.surface: Someone serves a long sentence before a reporter is released.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthened or laid out at full length, reaching as far as possible.

clue.text: Lived together, all be it ad hoc arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters means putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: A couple shared a home, albeit as a makeshift arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all be it' plays on albeit; only BE IT AD HOC is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple sharing a home without marrying are living as partners.

clue.text: One's never seen in the flesh

definitions.text: One's never seen in the flesh

parts.words: One's never seen in the flesh
parts.note: the bony frame inside a body is hidden by flesh, never visible while the body is alive

explanation.definitionFit: The bony framework is always covered by the tissue around it.

clue.text: Rhubarb disease caused by monarchy? Nonsense!

parts.note: the crown stands for the monarchy
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the idea that the royal family causes a garden blight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhubarb' also means nonsense, a tempting false lead; here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal infection that decays the base of rhubarb plants, a garden ailment.

clue.text: Where Japanese learn to chop by hand?

definitions.text: Where Japanese learn to chop by hand?

parts.words: Where Japanese learn to chop by hand?
parts.note: not a cookery class but somewhere a martial art's hand strikes are taught

explanation.definitionFit: A dojo teaching the Japanese martial art famed for its open-handed chops.

clue.text: A slinky creature who's happy in trousers?

definitions.text: A slinky creature who's happy in trousers?

parts.words: A slinky creature who's happy in trousers?
parts.note: refers to the old Yorkshire game in which a sinuous hunting animal is put down someone's trousers

explanation.definitionFit: A weasel-like animal used for hunting rabbits, famous in the British trouser-legging stunt.

clue.text: Stone remains, half dollar to see it all

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

indicators.note: half of the word dollar is taken, its final three letters

explanation.surface: Someone looks at a stone ruin and the last of their cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the second half of DOLLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed masonry: square-cut building blocks.

clue.text: On Scottish isle ian's cut back flowering plant

parts.note: Lewis is an island in the Outer Hebrides

indicators.note: the name is cut at its back end, losing its last letter

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A man named Ian has pruned a flowering plant on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American alpine perennial with bright blooms, named after the explorer Meriwether Lewis.

clue.text: A Texan tourist spot it's quite à la mode to visit

indicators.note: the place is found tucked within the words it visits

explanation.surface: A fashionable Texas landmark everyone is going to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'à la mode'.
explanation.definitionFit: The San Antonio mission where Texan defenders fell in 1836 is a famous sightseeing site.

clue.text: Worries wild animals

explanation.definitionFit: To pester or nag someone, and striped burrowing mammals of the countryside.

clue.text: Scold a good social worker when term starts…

indicators.note: starts tells us this word begins the answer

parts.note: the word term is used as written
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

explanation.surface: A nagging woman scolds a good social worker at the beginning of term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a carer but an insect; 'starts' puts TERM first.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrewish woman who nags is a harridan.

clue.text: …she'll go before may

parts.note: both a girl's name and the month which precedes the next one in the calendar

explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month comes ahead of the fifth, and is also a woman's name.

clue.text: The school returned a letter

indicators.note: returned means the school's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school sends back a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written message, a brief missive.

clue.text: On strand, poke about, looking for water insects

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone pokes about on a beach, searching for bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poke about' reads as rummaging, but 'about' rearranges STRAND POKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-legged bugs that skim across still surfaces.
